artifacts.synopsis: TE John Evans appealed Arizona Presbytery's vote to divest him of his office without censure under BCO 34-10, after he had already affiliated with the Evangelical Presbyterian Church in England and Wales and notified the Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC unanimously sustained the appeal and reversed the Presbytery's action, holding that Evans had withdrawn from Presbytery's jurisdiction under BCO 38-3a before the divestiture proceedings began, and instructed the Presbytery to record the irregularity, acknowledge his new membership, and remove his name from the roll.

artifacts.title: Myers v. Illiana Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Craig Sheppard complained that Highlands Presbytery erred by conflating judicial and pastoral procedures after finding a strong presumption of guilt, and by failing to institute process within one year as required by BCO 32-20. The SJC sustained both issues, holding that BCO 31-2 mandates process upon finding a strong presumption of guilt, and that Presbytery was debarred from prosecution because the alleged offense occurred in 2017 and timely process was never instituted; three members dissented on the BCO 32-20 issue, arguing it was not a true statute of limitations and that the matter was never a 'case of scandal.'

artifacts.title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Frazier complained that Nashville Presbytery erred in finding insufficient evidence to raise a strong presumption of guilt against TE Scott Sauls regarding his teaching on same-sex attraction; the SJC denied the complaint 20-0-1, concluding NP fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duties, accompanied by several concurring opinions raising procedural and exegetical concerns.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained TE Gonzales's appeal, reversing and annulling Great Lakes Presbytery's divestiture of him without censure under BCO 34-10, because GLP failed to follow the required procedural steps: it did not record a finding that Gonzales had habitually failed to discharge his official functions, nor determine that his neglect arose only from lack of acceptance to the Church, before proceeding to divestiture. The decision restored Gonzales to good standing in GLP while leaving open GLP's option to pursue proper process under BCO Chapter 31 or 34-10.
